context.title: The Descendants of Esau
context.summary: A record of Esau's wives, sons, clan chiefs and the kings of Edom, along with the native Horite clans of Seir.
context.background: Edom lay southeast of the Dead Sea in the rugged highlands called Seir. Edom and Israel remained neighbors and often rivals. Verse 31 lists kings of Edom 'before there reigned any king over the children of Israel,' which many readers take as a sign that the list was updated after Israel had kings.

customs.note: The KJV's 'dukes' are clan chiefs, leaders of family groups, not European nobility.

watchFor: Esau moves away because the land cannot support both brothers (vv. 6–8), as with Abram and Lot.
Amalek, ancestor of a later enemy of Israel, is Esau's grandson (v. 12).
Esau's line gets a full record before the story turns to Jacob's sons.

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Hivite
people.summary: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

people.name: Adah
people.summary: The first of Esau’s three wives, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Gen. 36:2, 4), called also Bashemath (26:34).

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Wife of Esau.

people.name: Elon
people.summary: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

people.name: Zibeon
people.summary: A Hivite (Gen. 36:2).

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5).

people.name: Bashemath
people.summary: The daughter of Ishmael, the last of Esau’s three wives (Gen. 36:3, 4, 13), from whose son Reuel four tribes of the Edomites sprung. She is also called Mahalath (Gen. 28:9).

people.name: Nebajoth
people.summary: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16).

people.name: Eliphaz
people.summary: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

people.name: Reuel
people.summary: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

people.name: Jaalam
people.summary: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

people.name: Jeush
people.summary: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

people.name: Korah
people.summary: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: The sons of Eliphaz.

people.name: Omar
people.summary: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz.

people.name: Amalek
people.summary: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Gen. 36:12; 1 Chr. 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Gen. 36:16).

people.name: Timna
people.summary: Lotan's sister.

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Grandson of Esau’s wife Basemath.

people.name: Korah
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz.

people.name: Lotan
people.summary: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

people.name: Seir
people.summary: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

people.name: Dishan
people.summary: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

people.name: Ezer
people.summary: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

people.name: Dishon
people.summary: Duke of Horites.

people.name: Lydia
people.summary: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13).

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

people.name: Onam
people.summary: Sons of Shobal.

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Discoverer of Hot Springs.

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Wife of Esau.

people.name: Akan
people.summary: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

people.name: Bilhan
people.summary: The sons of Ezer.

people.name: Zavan
people.summary: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

people.name: Aran
people.summary: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

people.name: Uz
people.summary: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

people.name: Bela
people.summary: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

people.name: Beor
people.summary: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: King of Edom, succeeded Bela (Gen. 36:33, 34).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Of Bozrah.

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Midian
people.summary: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

people.name: Baal-hanan
people.summary: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul.

people.name: Mehetabel
people.summary: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

people.name: Mezahab
people.summary: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

people.name: Jetheth
people.summary: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

people.name: Timnah
people.summary: A “duke” or sheik of Edom (Gen. 36:40).

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Edomite chief.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Teman.

people.name: Mibzar
people.summary: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: A chief of Edom.

people.name: Iram
people.summary: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: Seir
places.summary: The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea.

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Dinhabah
places.summary: Robbers’ den, an Edomitish city, the capital of king Bela (Gen. 36:32).

places.name: Bozrah
places.summary: The city of Jobab, one of the early Edomite kings (Gen. 36:33). This place is mentioned by the prophets in later times (Isa. 34:6; Jer. 49:13; Amos 1:12; Micah 2:12).

places.name: Midian
places.summary: An Arabian tribe descended from Midian. They inhabited principally the desert north of the peninsula of Arabia. The peninsula of Sinai was the pasture-ground for their flocks.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Masrekah
places.summary: Vineyard of noble vines, a place in Idumea, the native place of Samlah, one of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:36; 1 Chr. 1:47).

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: An ancient city on the Euphrates (Gen. 36:37; 1 Chr. 1:48), “Rehoboth by the river.”

places.name: Pau
places.summary: (Gen. 36:39) or Pai (1 Chr. 1:50), bleating, an Edomitish city ruled over by Hadar.

places.name: Esau
places.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).
